A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SMFA and S-MLLMUn Bench. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on two MLLMs at three forgetting ratios, including benchmark results, component ablations, parameter analyses, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, prompt attacks, evaluator validation, LoRA-rank sensitivity, and full-fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The refusal-trained memory forgetting adapter, few-shot retaining anchor, directional-conflict and relative-magnitude masks, and final merging procedure remain unchanged in Equations 4–11. Full fine-tuning is an additional experimental configuration of the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic-profile benchmark, facial and ophthalmic images, and image-understanding, image-memory, and text-memory tasks. V2 adds adversarial input scenarios through prefix injection, refusal suppression, distractors, and style injection in Table 3.

E2.justification: V2 adds Model Tailor and TIES-Merging throughout Table 1's model and forgetting-ratio comparisons and extends the appendix cases to these methods. The four original unlearning baselines remain, substantially broadening the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces three aggregate evaluation metrics and additional protocols using Gemini-3-flash, five human experts evaluating 1,080 items, LoRA ranks from 4 to 128, and full fine-tuning. The original two model backbones, forgetting ratios, and few-shot retain-set design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablation, masking-parameter sweep, and ophthalmic analysis, v2 adds prompt-attack robustness, alternative-judge and human validation, LoRA-rank sensitivity, and full-fine-tuning analysis. Existing appendix cases gain new comparator outputs, while the standalone example in v1 Figure 6 is removed.

E5.justification: V2 adds a statistical agreement assessment between human and LLM judgments, reporting an overall Pearson correlation of 0.948 in Table 5. Neither version reports repeated training runs, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: SMFA's shared Table 1 ROUGE-L and Fact Score values are retained, but v2 adds extensive comparator, aggregate, attack, evaluator-validation, rank-sensitivity, and full-fine-tuning results. For example, Table 6 reports retain-set understanding ROUGE-L of 0.640 for SMFA versus 0.105 for IDK under full fine-tuning. Most per-task Meaningful Scores are removed from Table 1 and replaced by overall scores.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.4 introduces mathematical definitions for aggregate understanding and retain-minus-forget memory scores. The SMFA equations remain unchanged, and neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim benign selective forgetting, introduce S-MLLMUn Bench and SMFA, and claim preservation of foundational visual understanding during targeted forgetting. V2 foregrounds the benchmark and describes SMFA as a strong baseline, without materially changing these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for TIES-Merging failure and full-fine-tuning overfitting, interprets evaluator agreement as supporting reliability, and acknowledges that some attacks weaken forgetting. Section 5.2 also qualifies the Meaningful Score claim from consistently highest to best or second-best. The central over-generalization explanation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-data availability link, the complete Meaningful Score judging prompt in Appendix D, and implementation descriptions for adapting Model Tailor and TIES-Merging in Appendix B. The original LoRA implementation, masking parameter, and refusal-label construction remain documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Model Tailor and Jailbroken and sharpens its discussion of limitations of knowledge editing and model merging for unlearning. TIES-Merging was already cited in v1; most other reference changes update bibliographic metadata or publication information.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the benchmark precedes the method, problem formulation moves into the benchmark section, and dataset descriptions move from Appendix A.1 into the main text. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are rewritten, related work gains numbered subsections, and the appendix structure expands.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Table 1 gains comparator rows and aggregate columns while losing per-task Meaningful Score columns; Tables 3–6 and new prompt and rank-analysis figures are added. Existing figures are relocated or rearranged, including the parameter plots, and v1 Figure 6 is removed.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, human and alternative-judge validation, and sensitivity and full-fine-tuning tests strengthen the empirical support; publishing the judging rubric improves reproducibility. Reporting weaknesses limit the gain: v2 does not reconcile its LLaVA 5% SMFA overall Meaningful Score of 7.98 with v1's per-category scores of 8.96–9.51, and Table 3 compares attacked SMFA with an unattacked IDK baseline.
